body: I'd like to have `public state: 'none' | 'started' | 'disposed'`, but I'm not sure how much `started` being used. At least, it's not documented https://www.algolia.com/doc/api-reference/widgets/instantsearch/js/.
started is used now, by Vue InstantSearch for example, but could we not introduce `state` instead of `disposed` now? (we can still set both state and started and deprecate `started`)
this code seems copied from a different point (if I remember it correctly constructor). Would it make sense to move it to .start in all cases, or is that a breaking change?
That sounds more future-proof.

it's similar to what we have in `use()`: https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/blob/25f41b2b3dcc71eb5b1c5598d98808d5cf2b023f/src/lib/InstantSearch.ts#L278:L302

but `use()` can be called either before or after `start()`.
maybe .use could be called somehow?

```suggestion
    state: 'none',
```

     mainHelper,

     started: false,
+    disposed: false,

body: edit: 'none' → 'initial'

I actually don't really understand why the middleware needs to be recreated, should the state not be set at `subscribe` (instead at function body now for routing middleware) so that it doesn't become stateful on creation, but on subscribe

Ah okay, about that part, initially I tried to make `subscribe()` be the place where it sets the state from the URL (Fix 1 or Fix 2 in the PR description). And it didn't work, and this was the final try. But reading your comment, I've become to not like making middlewares stateful on creation. Fix 1 and 2 are breaking the current behaviors. Do you have any other idea? If not, I should probably close this for now, and revisit it later for next major(, although as we've recently said, it's hard to prioritize these small/invisible tasks when working on major.)
why did moving the code to subscribe not work? I feel like that's the correct solution. Subscribe is called on start & restart right?

what if we move this to after the middleware subscribe happens? technically breaking behaviour, but I don't think it's something we defined as api (which order middleware happen in). Then we can move the initialUiState patch to before the init in subscribe of the middleware
That's suggested in fix 2, and let me give it another try. It got me many failed test cases here and there, but I didn't looked at them closely. It could be trivial, or not.
I guess the subscribe was expected to be called with a set ui state, which causes the tests to fail, although I'm not sure if that's really needed
this can continue to be read from the InstantSearch instance right?

But if subscribe() gets called multiple times, it could accidentally accumulate states.

For example, 

1. /search?hitsPerPage=3&query=abc

2. /search?query=def

but at the second visit, it will still get `hitsPerPage=3`, which is wrong.

The insights middleware used to rely on the helper to set/get user token. However, now that we get this `subscribe()` called before `mainIndex.init()` we no longer have access to the helper at subscribe(). We could setTimeout(fn, 0) but it will make the first query being fired without user token.

Anyway I don't like touching helper directly here, so changed the implementation to create a custom configure widget within the middleware to manipulate the search parameters.
This is technically a breaking change, but I don't think it will break anything in real life.
in that case the initial ui state can be captured here instead of making it an argument @eunjae-lee
yeah good point!
what about the configure widget instead of connector? It doesn't have any warnings or validation that would make the impact bigger
I'd create the arguments dynamically, but not the widget twice, that way you can add the widget with the known arguments *after* the if (or is that not possible?)
if the setUserTokenToSearch never was called, isn't configure undefined?

We add it in the beginning for `clickAnalytics`
https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/blob/6fba77c7167ee039ff6d3685616e7dfe64c81e8e/src/middlewares/createInsightsMiddleware.ts#L104:L106

Not sure which warnings or validation you mean. My initial thought on using the connector was to avoid any widget within middlewares. The connctors, middlewares, utils, etc can be shared across flavors, but we won't share widgets (although configure widget is renderless.)
I guess I'm not really sure what the flow should be. In that diff, aren't you adding the widget twice?
Yep, the widget is added multiple times now. Instead maybe create two widgets, one for userToken and one for clickAnalytics?
